answer: According to Section 40 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the right of private defence of the body commences as soon as there is a reasonable apprehension of danger arising from an attempt or threat to commit an offence, even if the offence has not yet been committed. This right continues as long as the apprehension of danger persists. Similarly, for property, the right of private defence commences when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property (Section 43(a)). Therefore, private defence begins with the perception of threat and concludes when that threat is no longer perceived.
summary_answer: Private defence starts with a reasonable apprehension of danger and ends when that apprehension ceases.
